config.title: List Rendering with map()

intro.title: List Rendering with map()
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays a list of items, such as a to-do list or a list of favorite foods. You will learn how to use the JavaScript `map()` method to transform an array of data into an array of React elements for rendering. The main technologies involved are React's JSX syntax and TypeScript for type-safe component development. This is a fundamental pattern in React for efficiently rendering dynamic lists of content.
intro.usecase: List rendering with map() is fundamental for displaying dynamic collections in real-world React applications. You'll use this pattern to render product listings in e-commerce sites, news feeds in social media apps, and search result panels. Developers constantly apply map() to build user interfaces like dashboard widgets showing metrics, navigation menus with dynamic items, and filterable data tables. Mastering this technique allows you to create reusable components that automatically update when underlying data changes.

objectives: Define a TypeScript interface to specify the shape of items in a list
Construct an array of objects that conform to the defined interface
Store the array in a React state variable using useState hook
Apply the map() method to iterate through each element of the array
Return JSX elements from the map() callback to render list items
Assign a unique key prop to each rendered list element
Utilize conditional rendering to handle empty arrays gracefully
Implement event handlers to modify the list state (add/remove items)
Control component re-renders by updating state with immutable patterns
Access array indices within the map() callback to display item positions
Modify list item properties through state updates and re-rendering
Construct a complete React component that renders dynamic lists from data

steps.instruction: Import React from the 'react' package to enable JSX syntax and React component creation.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the default export from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX.Element. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns a JSX element. For TypeScript, you can specify the return type as JSX.Element.
steps.seedCode:
import React from 'react';

// Create your App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a functional App component that returns JSX.Element.
successCriteria: The code defines a component named App (either as function App() or const App = () => {}) that returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the App component. This is the foundation of your React application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component is named exactly 'App' and returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've named it 'App' and it returns JSX.Element.

steps.title: Define an array of data
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a constant array named 'items' with at least 3 objects. Each object should have a 'name' (string) and 'id' (number) property.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript to define the array type. You can write: const items = [{ name: 'Item 1', id: 1 }, { name: 'Item 2', id: 2 }, ...];
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a typed array of objects ready to be rendered in the next steps.
successCriteria: The code should include a constant array named 'items' defined inside the App component, containing objects with 'name' (string) and 'id' (number) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a typed array of items. This will serve as the data source for list rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your array has the correct structure. Each object should have both 'name' (string) and 'id' (number) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the App component, define a constant array named 'items' with objects containing 'name' and 'id' properties.

steps.title: Return a wrapper div
steps.instruction: In your App component, return a div element that will wrap all the content. This div will serve as the main container for your component's UI.
steps.hint: Replace the existing return statement with a div element. Remember that in JSX, you need to wrap multiple elements in a single parent element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component returns a div element that will contain the component's content.
successCriteria: The App component returns a div element
The div is the root JSX element in the return statement
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned a div element from your App component. This provides the necessary wrapper for your component's content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your App component returns a div element as the main container. Check that your return statement has a div wrapping the content.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on returning a div element from the App component. The div should be the main container returned by the component.

steps.title: Add an h1 heading
steps.instruction: Inside the wrapper div in your App component, add an h1 element with the text 'My Items'.
steps.hint: Add the h1 element as a child of the div that's already being returned.

successCriteria: The h1 element is inside the div

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an h1 heading to your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an h1 element with the exact text 'My Items' inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The h1 element with text 'My Items' wasn't found inside the div. Check your JSX structure.

steps.title: Map over the array to generate list items
steps.instruction: Inside the <ul> element, use the map() method on your items array to generate <li> elements. Each <li> should display the name of one item from the array.
steps.hint: Remember to use curly braces {} to embed JavaScript expressions in JSX. The map() method takes a callback function that returns JSX for each element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The unordered list should now contain three list items displaying 'Item 1', 'Item 2', and 'Item 3'.
successCriteria: Return <li> elements from the map callback
Include a key prop on each <li>
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used map() to transform your array data into JSX list items. This is the core pattern for rendering lists in React.

steps.title: Add a key prop to each li
steps.instruction: Inside your map() callback, add a key prop to each <li> element. Use the current item string as the key value.
steps.hint: Add key={item} to your <li> element. This helps React efficiently update the list when items change.
